name: PatchProof fresh 40 — 2 human approvals, 38 agent approvals

cases.text: The carrier hasn't updated order 008264 since Tuesday, and the promised delivery date has passed. Tracking reference TRK-99142 is all I can see. Please tell me when my order will arrive.
cases.annotation_note: An overdue shipment and request for arrival information. Use the explicitly named order ID, preserve its leading zeros, and ignore the tracking reference.

cases.text: Your dispatch email lists order ZP-4831 and parcel code BOX-77490. The parcel has been at the depot for nine days instead of the advertised two. Can you check its delivery progress?
cases.annotation_note: Delivery is delayed and the customer asks for progress. The parcel code is not the order ID.

cases.text: I unpacked the desk lamp from order LM-6208 and found the glass shade shattered. Please return the amount I paid to my card.
cases.annotation_note: Physical damage is explicit. Returning the payment to the card is a refund request.

cases.text: Order 0003917 was the framed map. Its frame arrived split down one side. I'd like my payment reimbursed.
cases.annotation_note: A broken frame is damage; reimbursement is a refund. Preserve all leading zeros.

cases.text: The packing slip for order PN-1456 says a label printer, but the box contains a kitchen scale. Please send the label printer I purchased in place of this scale.
cases.annotation_note: The product differs from the one ordered. Sending the purchased item in its place is replacement.

cases.text: For order GX-9024 I selected a left-handed gardening glove set. You sent a right-handed set. Exchange these for the left-handed set, please.
cases.annotation_note: An incorrect product variant was supplied. An exchange for the correct variant maps to replacement.

cases.text: The receipt for order BV-7330 includes an installation fee, although I chose delivery only. Please explain why that fee was added.
cases.annotation_note: The disputed fee is a billing issue. An explanation is a clear action outside the named action enum; it is not a refund or progress request.

cases.text: Order EE-4182 was advertised with free shipping, yet my invoice shows a delivery charge. Could you give me a breakdown of how you calculated the total?
cases.annotation_note: The current request is to explain the charged total, not to report shipment status or return money.

cases.text: Order QF-2058 was due last Friday and still hasn't left your warehouse. Cancel the order; I no longer need the equipment.
cases.annotation_note: Overdue fulfilment is explicit. Extract cancellation without adding an inferred refund.

cases.text: The delivery appointment for order HT-8763 has been postponed three times. Please stop this order before dispatch and cancel it.
cases.annotation_note: Repeated delivery delays motivate an explicit cancellation request.

cases.text: The hinge on the case in order CR-5602 arrived snapped. Do not send another case. I want the purchase price refunded.
cases.annotation_note: Replacement is expressly negated. The current, affirmative request is a refund for damage.

cases.text: Order WD-3096 contains a dented water bottle. I am not asking for money back; send an undamaged bottle instead.
cases.annotation_note: The refund phrase is negated. The affirmative request is replacement of a damaged product.

cases.text: About the unexplained service charge on order SC-7418: my earlier message said 'refund it immediately'. That message is withdrawn. I now only want a written explanation of the charge.
cases.annotation_note: The quoted refund request has been explicitly withdrawn. The current action is an explanation.

cases.text: In yesterday's message about the duplicate debit on order DU-6814, I wrote 'explain the debit'. Disregard that request. Please refund the extra debit now.
cases.annotation_note: The old explanation request is withdrawn. The current request is to refund a duplicate payment.

cases.text: Order KC-5129 was supposed to contain a USB-C dock, but you sent a USB-A hub. Please refund it. Actually, I still need the dock: replace the hub with the ordered dock instead of refunding me.
cases.annotation_note: The customer explicitly supersedes the refund request with replacement. This is a resolved change of mind, not an unresolved conflict.

cases.text: You sent lined notebooks instead of the blank ones in order NB-2460. Exchange them, please. On second thought, forget the exchange and send my money back.
cases.annotation_note: The last instruction explicitly replaces the exchange request with a refund.

cases.text: My delivery is a week overdue. The only reference I have is tracking code PKG-882310; I cannot find the order number. Please check where the parcel is.
cases.annotation_note: The tracking code cannot stand in for the missing order ID. Preserve the clear delivery issue and status request; clarification of the target order is needed.

cases.text: The courier says my parcel was lost. Label reference SHIP-493802 is a shipping reference, not my order number, which I don't have. Please send the lost items again.
cases.annotation_note: No order ID is available. Resending the lost goods is replacement, while loss in transit is a delivery issue.

cases.text: Before I place an order, could you tell me whether the folding stand supports a 16-inch laptop?
cases.annotation_note: A clear general compatibility question needs no order identifier. It is outside the named issue and action categories.

cases.text: I haven't bought anything yet. Please explain which adapter I would need to use your travel kettle in Japan.
cases.annotation_note: A general product-information request is clear without an order. Missing order ID alone does not make every ticket ambiguous.

cases.text: The zipper on the bag in order BG-9357 is torn.
cases.annotation_note: The problem is clear but no response or remedy is specified. Unlike an explicit no-action request, merely reporting a problem does not resolve the missing action.

cases.text: Order CU-4271 arrived today. I ordered a set of measuring cups and found measuring spoons in the parcel.
cases.annotation_note: A wrong item is reported, but the customer does not say whether they want replacement, refund or another response.

cases.text: Order LP-8106 arrived four days late, but I have it now. This note is only for your records. I do not want any action or reply.
cases.annotation_note: The delivery issue is clear and the customer explicitly requests no action. Null action is intentional, so no clarification is needed.

cases.text: There was an incorrect tax charge on order TX-6642. Your team has already corrected it. I'm documenting the incident only; please take no further action.
cases.annotation_note: The past billing problem remains the issue type. The current request explicitly rules out further action.

cases.text: Order VF-3928 still hasn't shipped. Cancel it, but also keep that same order active for delivery. I want both instructions followed.
cases.annotation_note: Cancel and keep active are expressly simultaneous instructions. There is no correction establishing precedence, so the action needs clarification.

cases.text: The mirror in order MR-1825 arrived cracked. Refund the full payment, and do not refund any of that payment. Neither instruction replaces the other.
cases.annotation_note: The refund instruction directly conflicts with the prohibition. The text explicitly leaves the conflict unresolved.

cases.text: Both order AA-5813 and order AA-5819 contain the wrong size of filter. Replace the filters in both orders with the sizes I originally selected.
cases.annotation_note: Both orders are active targets, which the single order_id field cannot represent. The issue and shared requested remedy remain clear.

cases.text: An extra handling fee was charged on each of orders FF-2704 and FF-2705. Please refund the extra fee on each order.
cases.annotation_note: Two targeted orders cannot be encoded as one order ID. Both share a clear billing issue and refund request.

cases.text: My previous order OLD-1168 arrived without trouble and is not part of this request. The current order NEW-5470 is now two weeks overdue. Cancel NEW-5470, please.
cases.annotation_note: Only the current order is targeted. Mentioning an explicitly irrelevant past order does not require a null ID.

cases.text: Order HIST-3372 from last year was fine; no help is needed with it. This message concerns order NOW-6281: its ceramic tray is chipped. Refund the payment for NOW-6281.
cases.annotation_note: The customer distinguishes the irrelevant historical order from the sole current target.

cases.text: I was charged an extra service fee on one purchase. It could be order SB-3601 or SB-3607; I cannot tell which statement entry belongs to which order. Please refund that extra fee.
cases.annotation_note: The customer targets one order but cannot identify which. Preserve the clear billing problem and refund request without guessing an ID.

cases.text: One of the two boxes contained a broken timer. I mixed up the labels for orders TM-9046 and TM-9054, so I don't know which order the timer came from. Please replace the broken timer.
cases.annotation_note: A single affected order exists but its identity is uncertain. Damage and replacement are explicit.

cases.text: For order EM-7531, please change the engraving text from 'Mira' to 'Nora' before you make the pendant.
cases.annotation_note: This is a clear customization change, not damage, wrong item, billing or delivery trouble. The action is outside the named action enum.

cases.text: Please update the contact email for order CE-4880 to the new address I supplied in my account. No shipment or product problem is being reported.
cases.annotation_note: The intent is a clear contact-detail change. This extractor classifies the request; it does not require all details needed to execute the change.

cases.text: The bracket in order BR-6903 won't fit. I can't tell whether it is bent or you sent a different model. Please replace it with the correct working bracket.
cases.annotation_note: The customer cannot distinguish damage from an incorrect item. Preserve the clear replacement request but leave the issue uncertain.

cases.text: Something is wrong with the lens adapter from order LA-1572. It may be cracked, or it may be the wrong version; I cannot work out which. I want my payment returned.
cases.annotation_note: Two possible issue categories remain unresolved. The money-back request is nonetheless explicit.

cases.text: The lunch box in order LB-8405 arrived with a cracked lid. I want to return it, but I haven't decided between getting my money back and receiving a new one.
cases.annotation_note: Returning the item does not resolve the explicitly undecided refund-versus-replacement choice. Do not infer a refund from the word return.

cases.text: Order ST-2267 contained a narrow stapler instead of the wide one I bought. I will send it back. I'm still choosing whether I want the correct stapler or a refund, so I cannot specify that yet.
cases.annotation_note: The issue is known but the customer explicitly withholds the remedy decision. The intended return does not establish refund or replacement.

cases.text: The base of the vase in order VS-9784 was chipped when it arrived. I know your refund window has passed, but I am asking you to refund it anyway.
cases.annotation_note: Extract the explicit refund request without deciding whether policy permits it. A possible eligibility problem does not make this intent ambiguous.

cases.text: You supplied the wrong cable length in order CB-3148. I realise your exchange policy requires the original packaging, which I discarded. Even so, please replace it with the length I ordered.
cases.annotation_note: The requested replacement is explicit despite a possible policy obstacle. The task extracts intent and does not approve the exchange.
